record.paper_title: Completeness of sets of complex exponentials in convex sets: open problems
record.original_question: Let Λ = {λ_n} be a sequence of pairwise distinct complex numbers with 0 not in Λ and λ_n tending to infinity, and let Exp Λ = {exp(λ_n z)}. Let G be an unbounded convex domain in the complex plane that contains [0,+∞). With H(G) the space of continuous complex-valued functions on G that are holomorphic in the interior and carry the topology of uniform convergence on compact subsets, which sequences Λ make Exp Λ complete in H(G)?

evidence.quote: Let Λ = {λ_n}, n ∈ N, be a sequence of pairwise different complex numbers (points) in the complex plane C, 0 ∉ Λ, and λ_n → ∞ as n → +∞. Let X be a convex open or closed set on C. By H(X) denote the space of all continuous complex-valued functions on X which are holomorpic in the interior Int X of X (if Int X ≠ ∅) with the topology of uniform convergence on compact subsets of X. An exponential system Exp Λ = {exp(λ_n z)} is complete in X if the closure of the linear span of Exp Λ in H(X) coincides with H(X).
3) X = G is an unbounded convex domain in C, [0,+∞) ⊂ G.
(3-!) When X = G is an unbounded convex domain in C, the completeness problem was solved completely in [3, Theorem 2].

artifact.self_contained_problem: Let $\Lambda=\{\lambda_n\}_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ be a sequence of pairwise distinct complex numbers with $0\notin\Lambda$ and $\lambda_n\to\infty$ as $n\to\infty$. Associate with $\Lambda$ the exponential system $\mathrm{Exp}\,\Lambda=\{e^{\lambda_n z}:n\in\mathbb{N}\}$. Let $G\subset\mathbb{C}$ be an unbounded convex domain with $[0,+\infty)\subset G$. Denote by $H(G)$ the space of continuous complex-valued functions on $G$ that are holomorphic in the interior of $G$, equipped with the topology of uniform convergence on compact subsets of $G$. The system $\mathrm{Exp}\,\Lambda$ is said to be complete in $H(G)$ if the closure of its linear span in $H(G)$ equals $H(G)$. Give a complete characterization of those sequences $\Lambda$ for which $\mathrm{Exp}\,\Lambda$ is complete in $H(G)$.
artifact.status_search_result: The completeness problem for exponential systems in unbounded convex domains containing $[0,+\infty)$ is reported as having been solved completely (a full characterization is known), as indicated in surveys of completeness problems for complex exponentials in convex sets.

status_evidence.snippet: When X = G is an unbounded convex domain in C, the completeness problem was solved completely.
status_evidence.claim: The case of an unbounded convex domain containing [0,+∞) is fully resolved.
